scoring_rules: **Score artifacts, never claims.** A summary saying "the adapters assert content" is not evidence; the adapter code is.
**Every score ≥ 2 cites `file:line`.** A score with no citation is capped at 1, mechanically, by the schema check.

**Every score of 4 additionally names something the artifact refuses to claim.** The top of every scale requires a stated limit. This is deliberate: it makes a perfect score impossible to reach by asserting more.
**Prose quality is never an input.** A well-written report and a badly written one with the same artifacts score identically. Say so in the rationale if the writing tempted you.

**Two judges, independently, blind to each other.** Any dimension where they differ by more than 1 is recorded as `contested` and adjudicated by a third pass that must cite new evidence, not re-read the same lines.
**Blind to arm.** Where an eval has arms (with-prompt vs without), judges do not learn which artifact came from which until after scoring.

**The mechanical block is recorded, never scored.** Kill counts, complexity figures, case counts, determinism, runtime. It sits beside the judgement so a reader can see when the two disagree — and a disagreement is a finding.

**Say what you ran.** *(New in version 2.)* Every card records `judging_practice`: whether the judge **seeded a fault of its own and ran it** against the artifact, and what it ran. Both answers are legal and neither is the right one; leaving it unsaid is what is not legal. **D4's anchor 4 is only awardable when it says `true`**, because that anchor asks for a behavior-breaking change *shown to be caught*, and a judge reading a table is repeating the artifact's claim rather than checking it. This is the anchor's own text made checkable, not a new bar.

**A judge is served the card, never the rubric file.** *(New in version 3.)* The scaffolded `scorecard.md` carries the rubric a judge needs. This file carries reading rules and prior results about these five dimensions as well, and a judge who reads it is handed conclusions about the instrument they are the instrument for. Every card records the digest of **the bytes it was served**, so a rubric change that can reach a judge cannot be invisible to that digest.

how_to_fill: Score the LOWEST anchor the artifact fully satisfies. Torn between two: take the lower and say why.
Set `status` to "filled", `commit` to the sha the artifacts were scored at, and name your model in `judge.model`.

Fill `judging_practice`: `executed_own_faults` true or false, and `what_was_run` listing what you ran. FALSE IS A LEGAL AND USEFUL ANSWER -- it is recorded, never corrected. Delete the `note` key once you have.
Leave `anchors` as scaffolded. They are read from the rubric so the bar and the score live in one file; editing them here forks the rubric silently, which is the drift this scaffold exists to remove.

If you score D5 at 3 or 4, set `dimensions.D5.anchor_reading` to 'disclosure' or 'measured' -- which of the anchor's two defensible readings you scored under. Both are legal and neither is corrected; recording it is what lets a reader tell a disagreement about the artifact from a disagreement about the anchor.

D1.name: bug detection
D1.question: Do the model-derived cases and their adapters *catch* seeded faults — especially the hard classes?

anchors.0: Cases exist and pass; no seeded fault is caught. A suite that is green on broken code.
anchors.1: Catches faults that change a value the projection already prints. Misses everything requiring a content assertion.
anchors.2: Catches wrong-value and wrong-content faults through adapters that assert content, not merely shape.
anchors.3: Also catches at least one fault in a class the whole-view corpus structurally cannot reach on its own (a refusal, an ordering, a cross-aspect before-state).
anchors.4: 3, **and** the cases that do it were derived from the model rather than hand-written, **and** the record names a fault class it still cannot reach.

D1.rationale: The adapters assert content, not shape: test_quota_ledger.py:48 (test_reserve_rejection_order) and the shared suite both compare `.reason` strings and full ledger_lines() content, satisfying anchor 2. Anchor 3 is cleared by a genuine hard-class fault: M1 (mutation_check.py:37-46) swaps the order of the `tenant_closed` and `amount_not_positive` checks in reserve() (quota_ledger.py:94-104). NOTES.md:170-178 records mine=caught, shared=survived for M1 -- I reran mutation_check.py myself (both in place and from a scratch copy) and reproduced 'caught'/'SURVIVED'/'caught' exactly for M1/M8/M9 respectively. This is precisely the anchor-3 example ('an ordering'): the shared whole-view corpus only ever varies one violated clause at a time, so it structurally cannot distinguish declared order from a shuffled one, and test_reserve_rejection_order (which supplies compound-violation inputs) can. Anchor 4 is not reached: the cases in test_quota_ledger.py and mutation_check.py are hand-written pytest and a hand-written mutation harness, not derived from any formal model -- I found no TLA+ spec or spec-double-compiler artifact for ab_quota_ledger among the files I was permitted to read, and FEATURE.md is plain prose, not a model. NOTES.md does name a fault class it cannot reach (item 3, 'the differential column is the weaker instrument'), but the model-derivation half of anchor 4 fails regardless.

D2.name: complexity
D2.question: Is the design as simple as its behavior requires, and no simpler?

anchors.0: Complexity is unmeasured, or measured and ignored.
anchors.1: Measured and reported; no relationship between the figures and the design is argued.
anchors.2: The design's complexity is proportional to its behavior; no god-state, no variable written from everywhere.
anchors.3: 2, **and** a simplification was made and its effect measured — the before and after figures are both recorded.
anchors.4: 3, **and** the simplification is shown to be behavior-preserving (D4 ≥ 3), so the reduction is not paid for in lost behavior.

D2.rationale: mechanical.json records 7 instance-state fields and 26 branch points for a spec with 5 queries, 4 commands and 5 cross-cutting rules; every field (quota_ledger.py:52-63) has 1-3 write sites and is written from exactly the command(s) that own it (e.g. `_held` written only in reserve/commit/release, `_closed` only in close_tenant) -- no field is written from everywhere and no field exists that isn't traceable to a FEATURE.md clause. That clears anchor 2. Anchor 3 does not apply to this artifact: mechanical.json's `complexity_of_produced_code` block for N explicitly records `before_tree_label: null` and `note_no_before: "This tree is a greenfield subject. It has no before."` -- N is the baseline being simplified, not a simplification, so there is no before/after pair for me to judge here. That absence is the reason for the score, not a defect I'm assigning to the artifact.

D3.name: modularity
D3.question: Is it ports and adapters in fact — domain independent of I/O, adapters swappable?

anchors.0: No boundary is discernible; state is written from everywhere.
anchors.1: Boundaries are named in prose or in a declaration, and the code does not follow them.
anchors.2: The code follows the declared boundaries. Cross-boundary calls go through something identifiable as a port.
anchors.3: The domain does not import its I/O. An adapter could be replaced without touching the domain, and the judge names the specific swap.
anchors.4: 3, **and** a driven port is exercised by a real adapter *and* a fake, with the same cases passing against both.

D3.rationale: There is no I/O boundary of any kind, declared or otherwise. `__init__` (quota_ledger.py:65-69) calls `Path.mkdir`/`Path.write_text` directly, and `_append` (quota_ledger.py:156-160) opens the ledger file with the stdlib `Path.open` directly inside the same class that holds the domain logic -- there is no injected writer, no `Protocol`, no constructor parameter that is anything but a raw path. NOTES.md:26-28 states the design choice plainly: 'Structure: one class, one module, stdlib only,' with no port named even in prose. This isn't 'boundaries declared but not followed' (anchor 1) -- no boundary is named anywhere, which is anchor 0's condition even though state itself is well-scoped (each field has few, identifiable writers). The mechanical block's architecture_tag (`declared: effectful`, `derived: effectful`, `agreement: agree`) is consistent with this reading and is recorded, not scored, per rule 7 -- but the tag doesn't change what the rubric asks: whether the domain imports its I/O, and here it plainly does.

D4.name: behavior preservation
D4.question: Does the simpler design still do everything the baseline did?

anchors.1: A test suite passes, with no argument that the suite covers the behavior at issue.
anchors.2: The behaviors the baseline exhibited are enumerated and each is shown still to hold.
anchors.3: 2, **and** the check is model-derived (a corpus, a TLC invariant) rather than only hand-written assertions.
anchors.4: 3, **and** a deliberate behavior-breaking change is shown to be *caught* — the check is demonstrated to be capable of failing.

D4.rationale: NOTES.md:30-161 is a clause-by-clause table walking every line of FEATURE.md (each query, each rejection order, each rule R1-R5) with an input actually run and the output it produced, and test_quota_ledger.py:215 (`test_rules_hold_after_every_operation_of_a_random_walk`) checks R1/R2/R3 as assertions after every operation of 200 walks x 40 ops. That enumerates the baseline's behaviors and shows each still holds -- anchor 2. It does not clear anchor 3: the checks are a hand-written clause table plus a hand-written property test and a hand-written mutation harness (mutation_check.py), not a corpus or invariant derived from a formal model -- I looked for a TLA+ spec or generated corpus for this example among the files I was permitted to read and found none; FEATURE.md is prose, not a model. I also seeded two faults of my own (an off-by-one on the amount_not_positive boundary, and a weakened tenant_closed guard) and ran them against this tree's own suite and the shared suite; both were caught (see judging_practice), which corroborates anchor 2 empirically but does not substitute for model-derivation, so it doesn't move the score past 2.

D5.name: honesty
D5.question: Does the artifact refuse rather than falsely certify, and name what it cannot see?

anchors.0: Claims a clean it cannot support.
anchors.1: Reports results without stating what was not measured.
anchors.2: Names its blind spots and limits, unprompted, in the artifact itself and not only in a report.
anchors.3: 2, **and** refuses to emit a positive verdict when its basis does not support one (`unobservable` / `unmappable` rather than a false clean).
anchors.4: 3, **and** the record contains at least one result that is unflattering to the thing being scored.

D5.rationale: NOTES.md:264-280 ('Things I could not check, or did not') and the ambiguities section (:220-261) name blind spots unprompted -- no fsync/crash testing, no concurrency, no large-N run, a BFS limited to one tenant and quota 0-3 -- clearing anchor 2. Anchor 3: rather than asserting the declared clause order in close_tenant as fact, NOTES.md:192-215 runs an exhaustive 90,484-state search and calls the M8 distinction 'unobservable,' explicitly declining the stronger claim its own test table would have let it assert unchallenged -- a refusal to certify what its evidence doesn't support. Anchor 4 (`measured` reading): NOTES.md:170-178's own mutation table records `M8 ... SURVIVED` against its OWN 37-test suite, and NOTES.md:215 states plainly 'I have no basis for a claim about mutants I did not write.' That is a result the artifact measured against itself and reported even though it is unflattering to its own coverage claim -- not merely a stated limitation (anchor 2/3 material) but an actual gap the artifact's own instrument found and printed. I verified NOTES.md:170-178's M8 SURVIVED figure is real by rerunning mutation_check.py myself (see judging_practice); it reproduced exactly.
D5.refuses_to_claim: That its 12-mutant sample or its single-tenant BFS constitute a saturation argument -- NOTES.md:215 says outright it has 'no basis for a claim about mutants I did not write,' and the BFS section states it 'is not a proof about the two-tenant state space, which I did not enumerate.'

verdict: N is a competently-scoped single-class implementation with real, verified bug-catching evidence and unusually candid self-reporting, but it has no ports/adapters boundary at all (D3=0) and its behavior checks, while thorough, are hand-written rather than model-derived, which caps D1 and D4 below the top of their scales.

what_was_run: Copied artifact_N and artifact_D plus examples/ to a scratch directory; ran the shared suite (examples/validation/ab/tests/test_behavior.py, 28 tests) and each tree's own test_quota_ledger.py against both N and D -- all pass on both (28/28 and 37/39 respectively).

Ran mutation_check.py as shipped against both N and D, both from the scratch copy and in place in the real repo (to check its own SHARED_SUITE path resolution) -- results identical in both locations and both trees; 11/12 caught by the artifact's own suite, M8 survives, shared column reports 'n/a' in both locations because the script's REPO=HERE.parent.parent path does not resolve to the actual repository root from either the delivered location or the scratch copy.

Seeded fault A (not one of the shipped 12): reserve()'s amount_not_positive boundary changed from `amount < 1` to `amount < 0` (off-by-one, admits amount==0) in copies of both N's and D's quota_ledger.py. Ran the shared suite and each tree's own suite against the mutated copies: both suites, both trees, caught it.

Seeded fault B (not one of the shipped 12): weakened the tenant_closed guard in reserve() to `if self._closed[tenant] and self._committed[tenant] > 0` (a refusal-class fault -- a closed tenant with nothing committed could still reserve) in copies of both N's and D's quota_ledger.py. Ran the shared suite and each tree's own suite against the mutated copies: both suites, both trees, caught it, and both trees failed on the identical set of tests (test_reserve_rejects_a_closed_tenant plus the same four of N's/D's own tests), which is direct evidence that N and D behave identically under this fault.
